_note: One unit = one lesson path in five steps. Write 'God' (the Muslim view shows 'Allah'). Verses by ref only (shown from src/data/ayahs.json); hadith by id only (shown from src/data/hadith.json). 'about' lines are our own words, never a translation.

intro.muslim: On a cold, dark night, Musa saw a fire on a mountain and went towards it. There, in a blessed valley, his Lord called to him. Among the first things he was told was: worship Me, and establish prayer for My remembrance.
intro.curious: On a cold, dark night, Musa, known in the Bible as Moses, saw a fire on a mountain and went towards it. There God called to him. In the Quran's telling, among the first things he was told was to pray, to remember God.

muslim.situation: It's a busy Saturday. You're out with friends, the afternoon prayer time is ending soon, and nobody else is going to pray.

options.label: Skip it today and make up for it some other time.
options.feedback: Busy days are exactly when prayer slips. Next you'll see why it was given fixed times.

options.label: Find a quiet corner, pray quickly, and rejoin them.
options.feedback: That's the heart of it: a few minutes for God in the middle of a full day, at its time.

options.label: Pray once you're home, even though the time will have passed.
options.feedback: Better than leaving it, but prayers have their times for a reason. The teaching explains.

options.label: Feel guilty about it all evening but do nothing.
options.feedback: Guilt without action helps no one. Even a short prayer in a quiet corner counts.

curious.situation: You've promised yourself ten quiet minutes each day: no phone, just stopping to think. It's a busy Saturday, you're out with friends, and the day is nearly over.

options.label: Skip it today: there'll be time tomorrow.
options.feedback: That's how most good habits fade. See why Islam fixes prayer to times of day.

options.label: Step aside for a few minutes now, then rejoin them.
options.feedback: A short pause in a full day: that's close to how Muslims treat prayer.

options.label: Do it tonight, however late.
options.feedback: Better than nothing, but Islam fixes prayer to set times. The next step explains why.

options.label: Feel bad about it but do nothing.
options.feedback: Feeling bad doesn't build anything. A few minutes now would.

quran.about: At the valley, God tells Musa that He is God, there is no god but Him, so worship Him and establish prayer to remember Him.
Prayer has been prescribed for the believers at set times.
Seek help through patience and prayer, which is hard except for the humble.
Prayer keeps a person away from shameful and wrong deeds, and remembering God is greater still.
The believers who succeed are those who are humble and attentive in their prayer.

hadith.about: Praying five times a day washes a person clean, like bathing five times a day in a river.
What God loves most is what is done regularly, even if it is small.

insights.text: There are five daily prayers: at dawn (Fajr), midday (Dhuhr), afternoon (Asr), sunset (Maghrib) and night (Isha). Their times follow the sun, so the day is never long without a return to God.
Prayer is not only a duty but a help (2:45): something to lean on in hardship, not just one more task.

check.q: What was Musa told to do at the valley, according to 20:14?
options: Worship God and establish prayer for His remembrance
check.why: In 20:14 God tells Musa that He is God, so worship Him and establish prayer for His remembrance.

check.q: How many daily prayers do Muslims pray?
check.why: Five: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha.

check.q: What does 4:103 say about the timing of prayer?
options: Any time of the day is the same
It has been prescribed at set times
check.why: Prayer has been prescribed for believers at set times (4:103).

check.q: In the hadith, what are the five prayers compared to?
options: Bathing five times a day in a river
check.why: Like bathing in a river five times a day, the five prayers wash away sins.

check.q: According to 2:45, what should we seek help through?
check.why: Seek help through patience and prayer (2:45).

reflection.muslim: Which of the five prayers is hardest for you to keep? What one small change would help you keep it this week?
reflection.curious: What would change in your day if you stopped five times to remember what matters most?
